queue.li_title: DSCR Cash-Out Refinance Seasoning: 3, 6, and 12 Months
queue.li_desc: Why seasoning windows exist, what they cost investors, and what each window really costs a BRRRR investor.
queue.li:
The number that decides how fast a BRRRR investor scales isn't the rehab budget or the ARV. It's the seasoning window.

Most DSCR lenders require 6-12 months of ownership before a cash-out refinance can use the new appraised value. That's 6-12 months of your capital parked in a finished, rented property doing nothing.

Our window is 3 months. No lease required at closing — the market-rent appraisal qualifies.

On a $110K cash-in deal, getting your capital back at month 3 instead of month 6 is the difference between four cycles a year and two. At portfolio scale, that compounds into an entirely different growth curve.

Hard money buys the project: 6-24 months, interest-only, sized off after-repair value, funds the rehab, closes in as little as 72 hours.

DSCR holds the property: 30-year term from 7.00%, qualified on the rent it produces — no tax returns, no DTI.

The combined play is the standard BRRRR sequence: acquire and renovate on bridge, stabilize, refinance into DSCR at month 3, recycle the capital. One lender across both loans means the second underwrite starts warm instead of from scratch.

queue.li_title: Portfolio Loans for Rental Properties: One Note for 2–10 Rentals
queue.li_desc: How blanket loans qualify on combined rent, why the release clause decides your flexibility later, and when separate loans still win.
queue.li:
Somewhere around rental number five, the debt stack turns into a second job. Five loans, five payments, five insurance renewals, five lender portals.

The portfolio loan is the fix. One 30-year DSCR note secured by 2 to 10 rentals at once, qualified on combined market rent against combined PITIA. A strong property can carry a slightly weaker one inside the blanket, which is the quiet advantage over financing each door alone, where the weakest property gets declined on its own merits.

What actually improves:

Administration collapses. One payment, one escrow account, one renewal calendar. At eight doors that is hours a month back.

Closing costs collapse. One title order and one closing instead of eight, and the savings scale with the property count.

Equity works as a team. Aggregate loan-to-value is what gets underwritten, so a low-leverage property lets the pool support more than door-by-door caps would allow.

The clause that decides everything is the release. Before signing any blanket loan, know three numbers for every property in it: the allocated balance, the release price, and whether releases are capped per year. A portfolio loan with clean release terms is flexible. One without them is a roach motel.

And the honest counterargument. If you are about to sell several properties, separate loans exit cleaner. If one property is your crown jewel with outsized equity, blanketing it ties it up to subsidize the pool. Two properties barely justify the structure. The sweet spot starts around four.

Send the address list and the rents and the term sheet will show the whole pool priced as one.

queue.theme: DSCR requirements / no tax returns is not no requirements
queue.li_title: DSCR Loan Requirements: Credit, Down Payment, Reserves & Property Types
queue.li_desc: The checklist a DSCR underwriter actually works through, where the flexible lanes are, and the four things you will never be asked for.
queue.li:
The pitch on DSCR loans is that the property qualifies, not you. That part is true. It also gets misheard as no requirements at all, and that misunderstanding is what costs investors a closing.

Here is the checklist an underwriter actually works:

The ratio. Monthly rent divided by monthly PITIA, meaning principal, interest, taxes, insurance, and association dues. Most lenders want 1.0 to 1.2 or better for standard pricing, and a below-1.0 lane exists at adjusted terms for strong deals in appreciating markets. Rent comes from the lease in place, or from the appraiser’s market rent report if the property is vacant. No active lease is required at closing.

Credit. The practical floor is a 660 mid FICO, with meaningful pricing tiers at roughly 680, 700, 720, and 740 and above. If you sit a few points under a tier and a card payoff is about to post, waiting a month can genuinely pay.

Leverage. Purchases and rate-and-term refinances go up to 80% loan-to-value, cash-out up to 75%. Caps step down for lower credit tiers, lower ratios, and less common property types. An advertised maximum is the ceiling for a clean file, not a promise for every file.

Reserves. Three to six months of PITIA in liquid funds after closing, scaling with portfolio size. The eighth property draws more cushion than the first.

Property type. Single-family, 2 to 4 units, and warrantable condos are the core box. Short-term rentals, rural properties, mixed-use, and unique builds need a conversation rather than a rate sheet.

And the four things you will not be asked for: tax returns, employment verification, a personal debt-to-income calculation, and a cap on how many financed properties you already own. DSCR lenders never inherited the 10-property limit.

Loans run from $100K to $3M across 42 states, closed in your entity. The full breakdown is here.

Seasoning rules park your capital in a finished, rented property for 6 to 12 months before a cash-out refinance will recognize what the property is actually worth. Conventional lenders hold the 12-month line. Most DSCR lenders hold 6.

SLA Capital's DSCR cash-out refinances now carry no seasoning period at all. The day the appraisal supports the value and the rent covers the payment, the refinance can close.

No seasoning does not mean no scrutiny. Seasoning was always a proxy for one question: is the new value real? We answer that question directly instead of with a calendar.

The appraisal defends the number with closed comps at the finished condition tier.

The value creation gets documented: the purchase settlement statement, rehab invoices and paid receipts, before-and-after photos. Real work leaves a paper trail.

The DSCR math still governs. Market rent must cover the new payment at 1.0 or better, no lease required, and cash-out still caps at 75% LTV.

What it does to BRRRR math: the refinance timeline collapses to the project timeline. Buy in January, finish the rehab in March, and refinance in March rather than July or next January. At portfolio scale that is the difference between one or two cycles a year and three or four.

queue.theme: Build-to-rent financing / construction loan to DSCR relay
queue.li_title: Build-to-Rent Financing: How Investors Fund BTR From Dirt to Tenant
queue.li_desc: The construction loan that funds land and build, the DSCR refinance that converts it to a 30-year hold, and the build-vs-buy math.
queue.li:
The hottest corner of single-family investing is not buying rentals. It is manufacturing them.

Build-to-rent means constructing the house you intend to hold: brand-new product, premium rents, no deferred maintenance, and the developer's margin stays with you as equity. The financing is a two-loan relay.

Leg one is the ground-up construction loan. It funds up to 85% of land cost and 85% of construction cost on an 18 or 24 month term, with the budget released in draws as milestones complete and interest accruing only on the drawn balance. A lot you already own free and clear usually counts as equity toward your contribution. Underwriting wants approved plans, permits, a real GC bid with contingency, and documented liquidity. One BTR-specific note: build to a rental spec, with durable surfaces and market-appropriate finishes, not flip-glamour that rents no higher.

Leg two is the DSCR refinance that makes it a hold. Certificate of occupancy in hand, the finished home refinances into a 30-year loan qualified on market rent. No lease is required, because the appraiser's market-rent report qualifies a never-occupied home, and there is no seasoning period, so the refinance closes as soon as the CO and appraisal are in.

The build-vs-buy math with round numbers: a $70K lot, a $220K build, and $30K of soft costs and carry is $320K all-in. If the completed home appraises at $380K, building manufactured $60K of equity plus a house where nothing needs replacing for a decade.

The honest screen is the same as any spec build. The deal must pencil both ways, sell or hold, before you break ground. BTR is simply the version where holding was always Plan A.

queue.theme: Refinancing out of a hard money / bridge loan before maturity
queue.li_title: How to Refinance Out of a Hard Money Loan Before It Matures
queue.li_desc: The bridge-to-DSCR exit: the 90-day timeline, the DSCR test, what underwriting needs, and the options when the numbers are tight.
queue.li:
Every bridge loan has a built-in deadline, and the interest-only carry that felt cheap in month two feels different in month ten.

Whether the plan was always to hold or a soft sale market made holding Plan B, the exit is the same: refinance into a 30-year DSCR loan qualified on the property's market rent. The refinance itself takes a few weeks. The buffer around it is what is priceless.

The timeline that avoids extension fees:

90 days out, get the term sheet. Run market rent against the projected payment and know today whether the deal pencils.

60 days out, the application is in, the appraisal is ordered, and entity documents are current. That leaves slack for an appraisal that needs comp support or a title item that needs curing.

30 days out, you are in clear-to-close territory. If something is wrong, there is still room to fix it, or to negotiate an extension from a position other than desperation.

When the numbers are tight, work the fix list in order. Take a smaller loan that covers the payoff and skip the cash-out for now. Consider a 5-year interest-only structure, which often turns a 0.97 ratio into a 1.10. Challenge a light rent number with documented comparable leases. Ask about the below-1.0 lane for strong markets and strong borrowers. And if the hold math genuinely does not work, sell, which a 90-day head start keeps a choice rather than a forced outcome.

Two things make this exit cleaner at SLA Capital: no lease required, since the market-rent appraisal qualifies, and no seasoning period, so the refinance can close as soon as the value is defensible. We refinance bridge loans from other lenders too. 30-year fixed from 7.00%, before buy down, at the highest credit tier with DSCR 1.20+, on loans from $100K to $3M.
